blocks.text:
test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

      # gh-1724: the shard evidence uploads ride the gh-1412 one-shot retry —
      # run 39432336443 (tag v1.0.611) red'd shard 3 with every test GREEN on
      # a single transient `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: 404 artifact not
      # found` from GitHub's blob storage; the Quality gate followed
      # (`a leg is failure (test-core)`) and the release went red. Same
      # shape as the pty leg: the retry re-runs the SAME pinned action with
      # overwrite:true (a failed attempt leaves the artifact half-registered
      # — without overwrite the retry dies on "already exists"); a genuinely
      # dead endpoint still fails the shard loudly.
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        id: upload_core_coverage
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          name: coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2
      - name: Retry coverage upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: >-
          always() && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
          && steps.upload_core_coverage.outcome == 'failure'
        with:
          name: coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2
          overwrite: true

      # junit durations for the weekly shard-rebalance.yml (retention 7d so
      # a quiet week never starves it into the file-count fallback).
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        id: upload_core_junit
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          name: junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7
      - name: Retry junit upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: >-
          always() && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
          && steps.upload_core_junit.outcome == 'failure'
        with:
          name: junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7
          overwrite: true

  # Issue #551: the no-key integration legs (MockLlmServer scenarios, PTY
  # harness, no secrets, no network) run per-PR whenever test/integration/**
  # changes — the #538 rot class (legs breaking silently between releases,
  # discovered only at tag time) becomes a red PR at the commit that broke
  # them. Real-provider legs carry the `llm` …

Senior Developer Engineer specializing in root cause analysis and bug fixing ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## input_context_reading.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph INPUT_ORDER["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read input files FIRST before anything else"] I0["find input/ -type f | sort — list all available files"] I1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, deployment constraints, approved frameworks"] I2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/request.md — ticket description, requirements, solution design, diagrams"] I3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — existing discussion, prior decisions, linked info"] I4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/existing_questions.json — answered questions = binding requirements"] I5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — specifications already downloaded"] I6["6️⃣ Check for images in input/TICKET/ — *.png *.jpg *.gif *.svg"] I7["7️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent-KEY.md — parent story summary, description, ACs"] I8["8️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent_context_ba.md / sa.md / vd.md — BA/SA/VD context"] I0 --> I1 --> I2 --> I3 --> I4 --> I5 --> I6 --> I7 --> I8 end subgraph CONFLUENCE_RULE["Confluence pages in input/ — READ THEM, don't re-fetch"] C1["✅ DO: read input/TICKET/confluence/PageName.md"] C2["❌ DON'T: call dmtools confluence_* to re-fetch pages already in input/"] C3["✅ DO: read image files in input/TICKET/confluence/ — they are attachments from that page"] end subgraph ATTACH_RULE["Attachments — check before fetching via API"] A1["Search glob 'input/**/*.png' and 'input/**/*.jpg' — find pre-downloaded images"] A2["If image found locally → analyze it directly, no API call needed"] A3["If attachment NOT in input/ → use dmtools confluence_get_content_attachments "] A1 --> A2 A1 -->|not found| A3 end subgraph DMTOOLS_RULE["When to use dmtools for external data"] D1["ONLY if you need data NOT already in input/"] D2["dmtools jira_get_ticket KEY, dmtools confluence_search QUERY, etc."] D3["See instructions/common/dmtools_cli.md for full reference"] end INPUT_ORDER --> CONFLUENCE_RULE --> ATTACH_RULE --> DMTOOLS_RULE ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Bug ticket ready for fix]) --> READ["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read ALL input files FIRST — see instructions/common/input_context_reading.md"] READ --> RETURNED{Ticket returned to development?} RETURNED -->|Yes| PREV["Review previous PR diff and QA feedback in comments.md"] PREV --> RCA_RET["Write/Update RCA explaining why previous fix failed — see output_rules.md for rca.md format"] RETURNED -->|No| RCA_FRESH["Write fresh RCA from ticket description and linked_tests.md"] RCA_RET --> REPRO RCA_FRESH --> REPRO["Write a unit test that reproduces the bug. Run it — it MUST FAIL"] REPRO --> EXISTS{Test fails?} EXISTS -->|No| ALREADY["Check git history, current code, and linked tests.
⚠️ If linked test exists: verify it passes AND the test was created/updated BEFORE the fix commit — not after.
If bug is genuinely fixed — write outputs/already_fixed.json and stop"] ALREADY --> END_FIXED([End — bug already fixed]) EXISTS -->|Yes| BLOCKED{Fix requires external decision, secrets, or infra changes?} BLOCKED -->|Yes| BLOCK["Write outputs/blocked.json and stop — see output_rules.md"] BLOCK --> END_BLOCKED([End — blocked awaiting human input]) BLOCKED -->|No| FIX["Make minimum targeted fix for the root cause ONLY"] FIX --> VERIFY["Run reproduction test (must PASS) and full test suite (no regressions)"] VERIFY --> PASS{All tests pass?} PASS -->|No| ADJUST["Adjust fix and re-run tests"] ADJUST --> VERIFY PASS -->|Yes| GITSTATUS["Run git status and review every new/modified file"] GITSTATUS --> SECRETS{Sensitive or untracked non-code files present?} SECRETS -->|Yes| IGNORE["Add appropriate patterns to .gitignore"] SECRETS -->|No| SUMMARY["Write concise bug fix summary to outputs/response.md — see output_rules.md"] IGNORE --> SUMMARY SUMMARY --> END([End — post-processing handles git/PR]) ``` ## Returning from test-automation failure When this Bug has been sent back to development because a linked Test Case failed: 1. Read the `Failed Reason` field of every linked Test Case. 2. If the failure is caused by a missing token, missing permission, missing secret, or any other access/credential/infra issue that you cannot fix in product code, write `outputs/blocked.json` and stop. Do **not** try to code a fix for an access problem. 3. Only attempt a product-code fix when the failure is a genuine product regression. ## tdd_approach.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for Bug Fixes — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start with a clear understanding of the bug from RCA"] T1["RED: Write a unit test that REPRODUCES the bug
— must describe the exact failure scenario
— run it to confirm it FAILS"] T2["GREEN: Write minimum fix to make the reproduction test PASS
— simplest possible change
— do not refactor unrelated code"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— improve naming, remove duplication
— run full suite after every change"] T4{"More edge cases to cover?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for next edge case"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 T4 -->|No| DONE([Bug fixed with regression tests]) end subgraph RULES["Bug TDD Rules"] R1["❌ NEVER fix code without a failing reproduction test first"] R2["❌ NEVER write more code than needed to fix the bug"] R3["✅ Returned bugs: your fix must differ from the previous attempt"] R4["✅ If the bug involves a loop/collection, add a reproduction case with 2+ items, not only a single-item scenario — a single-item test can pass while multi-item logic is still broken"] R5["✅ Run the FULL test suite before finishing — no regressions allowed"] end TDD --> RULES ``` ## output_rules.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph OUTPUTS["Required outputs for bug development"] O1["outputs/rca.md — write FIRST, update as you learn"] O2["outputs/already_fixed.json — only if bug is genuinely fixed in current code AND tests pass"] O3["outputs/blocked.json — only if fix requires external input/credentials/infra"] O4["outputs/response.md — concise PR description (see formatting_rules.md)"] end subgraph RCA["rca.md format"] R1["## Root Cause Analysis"] R2["**Bug**: one-sentence description"] R3["**Root cause**: exact technical reason — file, function, line"] R4["**Impact**: what is broken and under what conditions"] R5["**Fix approach**: what needs to change and why"] R6["**Previous attempt**: PR #, what changed, why insufficient (only if returned bug)"] R1…

blocks.text:
test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

      # gh-1724: the shard evidence uploads ride the gh-1412 one-shot retry —
      # run 39432336443 (tag v1.0.611) red'd shard 3 with every test GREEN on
      # a single transient `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: 404 artifact not
      # found` from GitHub's blob storage; the Quality gate followed
      # (`a leg is failure (test-core)`) and the release went red. Same
      # shape as the pty leg: the retry re-runs the SAME pinned action with
      # overwrite:true (a failed attempt leaves the artifact half-registered
      # — without overwrite the retry dies on "already exists"); a genuinely
      # dead endpoint still fails the shard loudly.
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        id: upload_core_coverage
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          name: coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2
      - name: Retry coverage upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: >-
          always() && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
          && steps.upload_core_coverage.outcome == 'failure'
        with:
          name: coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2
          overwrite: true

      # junit durations for the weekly shard-rebalance.yml (retention 7d so
      # a quiet week never starves it into the file-count fallback).
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        id: upload_core_junit
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          name: junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7
      - name: Retry junit upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: >-
          always() && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
          && steps.upload_core_junit.outcome == 'failure'
        with:
          name: junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7
          overwrite: true

blocks.text:
test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

      # gh-1724: the shard evidence uploads ride the gh-1412 one-shot retry —
      # run 39432336443 (tag v1.0.611) red'd shard 3 with every test GREEN on
      # a single transient `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: 404 artifact not
      # found` from GitHub's blob storage; the Quality gate followed
      # (`a leg is failure (test-core)`) and the release went red. Same
      # shape as the pty leg: the retry re-runs the SAME pinned action with
      # overwrite:true (a failed attempt leaves the artifact half-registered
      # — without overwrite the retry dies on "already exists"); a genuinely
      # dead endpoint still fails the shard loudly.
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        id: upload_core_coverage
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          name: coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2
      - name: Retry coverage upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: >-
          always() && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
          && steps.upload_core_coverage.outcome == 'failure'
        with:
          name: coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2
          overwrite: true

      # junit durations for the weekly shard-rebalance.yml (retention 7d so
      # a quiet week never starves it into the file-count fallback).
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        id: upload_core_junit
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          name: junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7
      - name: Retry junit upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: >-
          always() && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
          && steps.upload_core_junit.outcome == 'failure'
        with:
          name: junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7
          overwrite: true

  # Issue #551: the no-key integration legs (MockLlmServer scenarios, PTY
  # harness, no secrets, no network) run per-PR whenever test/integration/**
  # changes — the #538 rot class (legs breaking silently between releases,
  # discovered only at tag time) becomes a red PR at the commit that broke
  # them. Real-provider legs carry the `llm` …

Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## blocks.text:
test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

      # gh-1724: the shard evidence uploads ride the gh-1412 one-shot retry —
      # run 39432336443 (tag v1.0.611) red'd shard 3 with every test GREEN on
      # a single transient `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: 404 artifact not
      # found` from GitHub's blob storage; the Quality gate followed
      # (`a leg is failure (test-core)`) and the release went red. Same
      # shape as the pty leg: the retry re-runs the SAME pinned action with
      # overwrite:true (a failed attempt leaves the artifact half-registered
      # — without overwrite the retry dies on "already exists"); a genuinely
      # dead endpoint still fails the shard loudly.
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        id: upload_core_coverage
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          name: coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2
      - name: Retry coverage upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: >-
          always() && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
          && steps.upload_core_coverage.outcome == 'failure'
        with:
          name: coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2
          overwrite: true

      # junit durations for the weekly shard-rebalance.yml (retention 7d so
      # a quiet week never starves it into the file-count fallback).
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        id: upload_core_junit
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          name: junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7
      - name: Retry junit upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: >-
          always() && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
          && steps.upload_core_junit.outcome == 'failure'
        with:
          name: junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7
          overwrite: true

  # Issue #551: the no-key integration legs (MockLlmServer scenarios, PTY
  # harness, no secrets, no network) run per-PR whenever test/integration/**
  # changes — the #538 rot class (legs breaking silently between releases,
  # discovered only at tag time) becomes a red PR at the commit that broke
  # them. Real-provider legs carry the `llm` …

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## input_context_reading.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph INPUT_ORDER["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read input files FIRST before anything else"] I0["find input/ -type f | sort — list all available files"] I1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, deployment constraints, approved frameworks"] I2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/request.md — ticket description, requirements, solution design, diagrams"] I3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — existing discussion, prior decisions, linked info"] I4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/existing_questions.json — answered questions = binding requirements"] I5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — specifications already downloaded"] I6["6️⃣ Check for images in input/TICKET/ — *.png *.jpg *.gif *.svg"] I7["7️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent-KEY.md — parent story summary, description, ACs"] I8["8️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent_context_ba.md / sa.md / vd.md — BA/SA/VD context"] I0 --> I1 --> I2 --> I3 --> I4 --> I5 --> I6 --> I7 --> I8 end subgraph CONFLUENCE_RULE["Confluence pages in input/ — READ THEM, don't re-fetch"] C1["✅ DO: read input/TICKET/confluence/PageName.md"] C2["❌ DON'T: call dmtools confluence_* to re-fetch pages already in input/"] C3["✅ DO: read image files in input/TICKET/confluence/ — they are attachments from that page"] end subgraph ATTACH_RULE["Attachments — check before fetching via API"] A1["Search glob 'input/**/*.png' and 'input/**/*.jpg' — find pre-downloaded images"] A2["If image found locally → analyze it directly, no API call needed"] A3["If attachment NOT in input/ → use dmtools confluence_get_content_attachments "] A1 --> A2 A1 -->|not found| A3 end subgraph DMTOOLS_RULE["When to use dmtools for external data"] D1["ONLY if you need data NOT already in input/"] D2["dmtools jira_get_ticket KEY, dmtools confluence_search QUERY, etc."] D3["See instructions/common/dmtools_cli.md for full reference"] end INPUT_ORDER --> CONFLUENCE_RULE --> ATTACH_RULE --> DMTOOLS_RULE ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Bug ticket ready for fix]) --> READ["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read ALL input files FIRST — see instructions/common/input_context_reading.md"] READ --> RETURNED{Ticket returned to development?} RETURNED -->|Yes| PREV["Review previous PR diff and QA feedback in comments.md"] PREV --> RCA_RET["Write/Update RCA explaining why previous fix failed — see output_rules.md for rca.md format"] RETURNED -->|No| RCA_FRESH["Write fresh RCA from ticket description and linked_tests.md"] RCA_RET --> REPRO RCA_FRESH --> REPRO["Write a unit test that reproduces the bug. Run it — it MUST FAIL"] REPRO --> EXISTS{Test fails?} EXISTS -->|No| ALREADY["Check git history, current code, and linked tests.
⚠️ If linked test exists: verify it passes AND the test was created/updated BEFORE the fix commit — not after.
If bug is genuinely fixed — write outputs/already_fixed.json and stop"] ALREADY --> END_FIXED([End — bug already fixed]) EXISTS -->|Yes| BLOCKED{Fix requires external decision, secrets, or infra changes?} BLOCKED -->|Yes| BLOCK["Write outputs/blocked.json and stop — see output_rules.md"] BLOCK --> END_BLOCKED([End — blocked awaiting human input]) BLOCKED -->|No| FIX["Make minimum targeted fix for the root cause ONLY"] FIX --> VERIFY["Run reproduction test (must PASS) and full test suite (no regressions)"] VERIFY --> PASS{All tests pass?} PASS -->|No| ADJUST["Adjust fix and re-run tests"] ADJUST --> VERIFY PASS -->|Yes| GITSTATUS["Run git status and review every new/modified file"] GITSTATUS --> SECRETS{Sensitive or untracked non-code files present?} SECRETS -->|Yes| IGNORE["Add appropriate patterns to .gitignore"] SECRETS -->|No| SUMMARY["Write concise bug fix summary to outputs/response.md — see output_rules.md"] IGNORE --> SUMMARY SUMMARY --> END([End — post-processing handles git/PR]) ``` ## Returning from test-automation failure When this Bug has been sent back to development because a linked Test Case failed: 1. Only attempt a product-code fix when the failure is a genuine product regression. ## tdd_approach.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for Bug Fixes — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start with a clear understanding of the bug from RCA"] T1["RED: Write a unit test that REPRODUCES the bug
— must describe the exact failure scenario
— run it to confirm it FAILS"] T2["GREEN: Write minimum fix to make the reproduction test PASS
— simplest possible change
— do not refactor unrelated code"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— improve naming, remove duplication
— run full suite after every change"] T4{"More edge cases to cover?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for next edge case"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 T4 -->|No| DONE([Bug fixed with regression tests]) end subgraph RULES["Bug TDD Rules"] R1["❌ NEVER fix code without a failing reproduction test first"] R2["❌ NEVER write more code than needed to fix the bug"] R3["✅ Returned bugs: your fix must differ from the previous attempt"] R4["✅ If the bug involves a loop/collection, add a reproduction case with 2+ items, not only a single-item scenario — a single-item test can pass while multi-item logic is still broken"] R5["✅ Run the FULL test suite before finishing — no regressions allowed"] end TDD --> RULES ``` ## output_rules.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph OUTPUTS["Required outputs for bug development"] O1["outputs/rca.md — write FIRST, update as you learn"] O2["outputs/already_fixed.json — only if bug is genuinely fixed in current code AND tests pass"] O3["outputs/blocked.json — only if fix requires external input/credentials/infra"] O4["outputs/response.md — concise PR description (see formatting_rules.md)"] end subgraph RCA["rca.md format"] R1["## Root Cause Analysis"] R2["**Bug**: one-sentence description"] R3["**Root cause**: exact technical reason — file, function, line"] R4["**Impact**: what is broken and under what conditions"] R5["**Fix approach**: what needs to change and why"] R6["**Previous attempt**: PR #, what changed, why insufficient (only if returned bug)"] R1…

blocks.text:
test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')

          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

      # gh-1724: the shard evidence uploads ride the gh-1412 one-shot retry —
      # run 39432336443 (tag v1.0.611) red'd shard 3 with every test GREEN on
      # a single transient `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: 404 artifact not
      # found` from GitHub's blob storage; the Quality gate followed
      # (`a leg is failure (test-core)`) and the release went red. Same
      # shape as the pty leg: the retry re-runs the SAME pinned action with
      # overwrite:true (a failed attempt leaves the artifact half-registered
      # — without overwrite the retry dies on "already exists"); a genuinely
      # dead endpoint still fails the shard loudly.
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        id: upload_core_coverage
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          name: coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info

      - name: Retry coverage upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: >-
          always() && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
          && steps.upload_core_coverage.outcome == 'failure'
        with:
          name: coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2
          overwrite: true

      # junit durations for the weekly shard-rebalance.yml (retention 7d so
      # a quiet week never starves it into the file-count fallback).
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        id: upload_core_junit
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          name: junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7
      - name: Retry junit upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: >-
          always() && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
          && steps.upload_core_junit.outcome == 'failure'
        with:
          name: junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7
          overwrite: true

**Red run (01:15, tag):** shard 2 exceeded 720s — so it ran ≥ ~200s slower than the green run. All other shards were FASTER in the red run than the green run (shard 1: 01:20:12→01:29:08 = 536s vs 499s green — actually slightly slower; shard 3: 48s vs 460s; shard 0: 485s vs 515s).

So in the red run, shards 0/1/3 took 485/536/48s and shard 2 blew past 720s. The distribution of wall times in green: 525/499/460/515 — all four shards are tightly packed around ~500s, i.e. the 12-min timeout (720s) has only ~40% headroom over the balanced shard duration.

The top file in shard 2: `agent_cli_stall_window_notice_test.dart` at 91.5s summed (but this is summed per-case; wall time with concurrency differs). Also `provider_export_test.dart` 54s, `release_flow_race_test.dart` 31s.

Key questions for root cause:
1. Was the red run's shard 2 simply a slow runner (ambient noise)? Evidence: this repo has a "Hostile ambient env" leg and a "Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)" job. Let me check what the watchdog does — if it retriggers degraded legs, why was it skipped?
2. Is there any test in shard 2 that hangs/flakes with unbounded duration? `agent_cli_stall_window_notice_test.dart` — stall window notice tests — these involve real timers. A hang in one test can eat the entire budget. The cancelled-at log showed tests near the end of the alphabet: release_flow_race_test.dart, scripts/ios_build_failure_classifier_test.dart, secrets/secure_key_save_degradation_test.dart...

Senior Developer Engineer specializing in root cause analysis and bug fixing ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## input_context_reading.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph INPUT_ORDER["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read input files FIRST before anything else"] I0["find input/ -type f | sort — list all available files"] I1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, deployment constraints, approved frameworks"] I2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/request.md — ticket description, requirements, solution design, diagrams"] I3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — existing discussion, prior decisions, linked info"] I4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/existing_questions.json — answered questions = binding requirements"] I5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — specifications already downloaded"] I6["6️⃣ Check for images in input/TICKET/ — *.png *.jpg *.gif *.svg"] I7["7️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent-KEY.md — parent story summary, description, ACs"] I8["8️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent_context_ba.md / sa.md / vd.md — BA/SA/VD context"] I0 --> I1 --> I2 --> I3 --> I4 --> I5 --> I6 --> I7 --> I8 end subgraph CONFLUENCE_RULE["Confluence pages in input/ — READ THEM, don't re-fetch"] C1["✅ DO: read input/TICKET/confluence/PageName.md"] C2["❌ DON'T: call dmtools confluence_* to re-fetch pages already in input/"] C3["✅ DO: read image files in input/TICKET/confluence/ — they are attachments from that page"] end subgraph ATTACH_RULE["Attachments — check before fetching via API"] A1["Search glob 'input/**/*.png' and 'input/**/*.jpg' — find pre-downloaded images"] A2["If image found locally → analyze it directly, no API call needed"] A3["If attachment NOT in input/ → use dmtools confluence_get_content_attachments "] A1 --> A2 A1 -->|not found| A3 end subgraph DMTOOLS_RULE["When to use dmtools for external data"] D1["ONLY if you need data NOT already in input/"] D2["dmtools jira_get_ticket KEY, dmtools confluence_search QUERY, etc."] D3["See instructions/common/dmtools_cli.md for full reference"] end INPUT_ORDER --> CONFLUENCE_RULE --> ATTACH_RULE --> DMTOOLS_RULE ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Bug ticket ready for fix]) --> READ["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read ALL input files FIRST — see instructions/common/input_context_reading.md"] READ --> RETURNED{Ticket returned to development?} RETURNED -->|Yes| PREV["Review previous PR diff and QA feedback in comments.md"] PREV --> RCA_RET["Write/Update RCA explaining why previous fix failed — see output_rules.md for rca.md format"] RETURNED -->|No| RCA_FRESH["Write fresh RCA from ticket description and linked_tests.md"] RCA_RET --> REPRO RCA_FRESH --> REPRO["Write a unit test that reproduces the bug. Run it — it MUST FAIL"] REPRO --> EXISTS{Test fails?} EXISTS -->|No| ALREADY["Check git history, current code, and linked tests.
⚠️ If linked test exists: verify it passes AND the test was created/updated BEFORE the fix commit — not after.
If bug is genuinely fixed — write outputs/already_fixed.json and stop"] ALREADY --> END_FIXED([End — bug already fixed]) EXISTS -->|Yes| BLOCKED{Fix requires external decision, secrets, or infra changes?} BLOCKED -->|Yes| BLOCK["Write outputs/blocked.json and stop — see output_rules.md"] BLOCK --> END_BLOCKED([End — blocked awaiting human input]) BLOCKED -->|No| FIX["Make minimum targeted fix for the root cause ONLY"] FIX --> VERIFY["Run reproduction test (must PASS) and full test suite (no regressions)"] VERIFY --> PASS{All tests pass?} PASS -->|No| ADJUST["Adjust fix and re-run tests"] ADJUST --> VERIFY PASS -->|Yes| GITSTATUS["Run git status and review every new/modified file"] GITSTATUS --> SECRETS{Sensitive or untracked non-code files present?} SECRETS -->|Yes| IGNORE["Add appropriate patterns to .gitignore"] SECRETS -->|No| SUMMARY["Write concise bug fix summary to outputs/response.md — see output_rules.md"] IGNORE --> SUMMARY SUMMARY --> END([End — post-processing handles git/PR]) ``` ## Returning from test-automation failure When this Bug has been sent back to development because a linked Test Case failed: 1. Read the `Failed Reason` field of every linked Test Case. 2. If the failure is caused by a missing token, missing permission, missing secret, or any other access/credential/infra issue that you cannot fix in product code, write `outputs/blocked.json` and stop. Do **not** try to code a fix for an access problem. 3. Only attempt a product-code fix when the failure is a genuine product regression. ## tdd_approach.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for Bug Fixes — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start with a clear understanding of the bug from RCA"] T1["RED: Write a unit test that REPRODUCES the bug
— must describe the exact failure scenario
— run it to confirm it FAILS"] T2["GREEN: Write minimum fix to make the reproduction test PASS
— simplest possible change
— do not refactor unrelated code"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— improve naming, remove duplication
— run full suite after every change"] T4{"More edge cases to cover?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for next edge case"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 T4 -->|No| DONE([Bug fixed with regression tests]) end subgraph RULES["Bug TDD Rules"] R1["❌ NEVER fix code without a failing reproduction test first"] R2["❌ NEVER write more code than needed to fix the bug"] R3["✅ Returned bugs: your fix must differ from the previous attempt"] R4["✅ If the bug involves a loop/collection, add a reproduction case with 2+ items, not only a single-item scenario — a single-item test can pass while multi-item logic is still broken"] R5["✅ Run the FULL test suite before finishing — no regressions allowed"] end TDD --> RULES ``` ## output_rules.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph OUTPUTS["Required outputs for bug development"] O1["outputs/rca.md — write FIRST, update as you learn"] O2["outputs/already_fixed.json — only if bug is genuinely fixed in current code AND tests pass"] O3["outputs/blocked.json — only if fix requires external input/credentials/infra"] O4["outputs/response.md — concise PR description (see formatting_rules.md)"] end subgraph RCA["rca.md format"] R1["## Root Cause Analysis"] R2["**Bug**: one-sentence description"] R3["**Root cause**: exact technical reason — file, function, line"] R4["**Impact**: what is broken and under what conditions"] R5["**Fix approach**: what needs to change and why"] R6["**Previous attempt**: PR #, what changed, why insufficient (only if returned bug)"] R1…

blocks.text:
test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

      # gh-1724: the shard evidence uploads ride the gh-1412 one-shot retry —
      # run 39432336443 (tag v1.0.611) red'd shard 3 with every test GREEN on
      # a single transient `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: 404 artifact not
      # found` from GitHub's blob storage; the Quality gate followed
      # (`a leg is failure (test-core)`) and the release went red. Same
      # shape as the pty leg: the retry re-runs the SAME pinned action with
      # overwrite:true (a failed attempt leaves the artifact half-registered
      # — without overwrite the retry dies on "already exists"); a genuinely
      # dead endpoint still fails the shard loudly.
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        id: upload_core_coverage
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          name: coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2
      - name: Retry coverage upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: >-
          always() && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
          && steps.upload_core_coverage.outcome == 'failure'
        with:
          name: coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2
          overwrite: true

      # junit durations for the weekly shard-rebalance.yml (retention 7d so
      # a quiet week never starves it into the file-count fallback).
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        id: upload_core_junit
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          name: junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7
      - name: Retry junit upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: >-
          always() && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
          && steps.upload_core_junit.outcome == 'failure'
        with:
          name: junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7
          overwrite: true

  # harness, no secrets, no network) run per-PR whenever test/integration/**
  # changes — the #538 rot class (legs breaking silently between releases,
  # discovered only at tag time) becomes a red PR at the commit that broke
  # them. Real-provider legs carry the `llm` …

Found the root cause of the 5-minute delay:

1. **`Pub cache` step: "Cache not found for input keys: pub-Linux-, pub-Linux-"** — 01:19:33 → 01:21:46 = **2m13s spent on a cache lookup that MISED**. Also notice the key: `pub-Linux-` with an EMPTY hash — `hashFiles('pubspec.lock')` evaluated to EMPTY! The cache key should be `pub-Linux-<hash>`. An empty hashFiles means pubspec.lock wasn't found at evaluation time... Actually the key template is `pub-${ runner.os }}-${ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}`. In the failing run, key = "pub-Linux-" (empty hash) — the restore key fallback "pub-Linux-" also empty. So the pub cache NEVER hits — every run re-downloads the entire pub cache.

Wait — but is that also true in the green run? Let me check. And `dart pub get` at 01:21:46 took... "Resolving dependencies..." at 01:21:46, next step at 01:21:49 — only 2.5s?? That means pub get used an existing global pub cache (from the runner image? or...). Hmm, that's fast because the dependencies were already in ~/.pub-cache on the runner?? No wait — cache not found... but pub get finished in 2.5s. Suspicious. Unless the runner image has a warm pub cache, or pub get resolved quickly from the hosted CDN with a warm... 2.5s is too fast for a cold pub get of a big dep tree.

2. **`Native-assets hook cache`: "Cache not found"** — 01:21:49 → 01:24:02 = **2m13s ALSO on a cache MISS**. Key: `hooks-shared-Linux-<arch>-[REDACTED]` (redacted = the hash). The native-assets hook cache misses → hooks (build hooks) run from scratch inside dart test startup, which is the expensive part.

So the cancelled run: **both caches missed** (pub + hooks), adding ~4.5 minutes of setup before dart test even started. Then tests ran at an OK pace but hit the 12-min wall 92% through.

Also compare: the failing run's pub cache key shows `pub-Linux-` — hashFiles('pubspec.lock') EMPTY. Why? Because `hashFiles` is evaluated... the pubspec.lock IS in the repo. Hmm — `hashFiles('pubspec.lock')` searches relative to GITHUB_WORKSPACE. It should work. UNLESS the checkout happens... no, checkout runs before. 

Wait, actually look: "Cache not found for input keys: pub-Linux-, pub-Linux-". BOTH the primary key AND the restore key show empty hash. In the redacted hooks key: `hooks-shared-Linux-<arch>-[REDACTED:High Entropy String]` — the hash IS present there (redacted in logs). So hashFiles works for the hooks cache but shows empty for pub?? Odd. Unless the pub cache step's log line is "pub-Linux-, pub-Linux-" because hashFiles('pubspec.lock') returned empty — is pubspec.lock at repo root? Yes (I saw pubspec.yaml, pubspec_overides.yaml... let me check pubspec.lock exists).

Hmm — from the earlier ls: pubspec.yaml exists, pubspec_overides.yaml exists... I didn't see pubspec.lock in the root listing! Let me check: the root listing shows `pubspec.yaml`, `pubspec_overides.yaml`, `pubspec.lock`? Scrolling: "pubspec.yaml", "pubspec_overides.yaml" — NO pubspec.lock visible in root! Let me verify. If pubspec.lock is gitignored (generated by pub get), then hashFiles('pubspec.lock') = '' ALWAYS, and the cache key is always `pub-Linux-` — a CONSTANT. Then the cache should HIT on the second run of the same branch (restore-keys fallback `pub-Linux-` would match the saved `pub-Linux-` entry)... but it says "Cache not found", meaning no entry with key `pub-Linux-` was ever SAVED. The save happens in the post-job step — but the job got CANCELED, so the post-cache-save never ran... but that's only for THIS run.

But wait — this same job has been running for days with the same key scheme. Why would the cache be missing? Because the cache is scoped to the BRANCH (default: caches are branch-scoped; the default branch's caches are accessible to all branches). The v1.0.621 tag run — caches saved on tag refs... For a tag-triggered run, GitHub Actions cache restore falls back to the default branch's caches. If main's runs save `pub-Linux-<hash>`... they'd save `pub-Linux-` (same empty hash) — should be found!

Hmm wait, actually let me re-check: is pubspec.lock in .gitignore? The repo has `.pubignore`... and a `check_lockfiles_gate` test and "Lockfile smoke" job — suggesting lockfiles are managed. Let me just check the green run's cache step logs to compare — the green run's shard 2 was 525s total, so its setup must have been much faster (cache hits).

Actually — wait. Let me reconsider. In the green run, did the pub cache hit? Let me download the green run's shard 2 log and check the same markers. This will show whether cache misses are systematic (infra bug → every run pays) or specific to the tag run (e.g. tag runs have no branch cache scope... actually tags DO fall back to default-branch caches).

Hmm, but actually there's an important GitHub Actions subtlety: **caches created on a tag ref ARE accessible, and tag runs can restore caches saved by the default branch**. So a miss on the tag run is unusual if main runs saved the same key.

UNLESS: the cache was EVICTED (10GB limit) — with ~57 workflows running continuously (this repo has MANY workflows and runs every 10 min: sm tick, kickers...), cache eviction pressure is high. With `retention`/eviction, keys like `pub-Linux-` (no hash) get saved repeatedly (each save overwrites/creates new cache entry with same key — actually saving with an existing key SKIPS saving ("Cache already exists")... and with `restore-keys` partial matches).

Let me compare with the green run logs to see if caches hit there. This is the crux: if green had cache hits and red had misses, the root cause is "cache miss on the tag run → +4.5min setup → blew the 12-min budget that was sized for warm-cache runs."

- (b) fix the cache key (include a real lockfile hash / make pub cache hit).
- (c) make the shards 3 instead of 4, or rebalance.
